chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, or someone else, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Abdul Hamid al-Wasiti, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Muhammad, Islam is a level.' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'And faith is a level over Islam.' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'And piety is a level over faith.' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'And conviction is a level over piety.' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'So people have not been given anything less than conviction, and you are merely holding onto the lowest level of Islam. Beware lest it slip from your hands.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual hierarchy of Islam, faith, piety, and conviction according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) outlines a four-tier spiritual hierarchy—Islam, Iman, Taqwa, and Yaqin—highlighting that while outward submission is common, true certainty (yaqin) is the rarest and most essential state of the heart. This classification underscores the Shia emphasis on moving beyond mere ritualistic adherence to a profound, internalized conviction, warning believers against settling for the superficial level of Islam. The narration serves as a critical reminder that spiritual perfection requires deepening one's faith from action to inner certainty.
